title: This, That, These, Those
summary: Learn how to point to things that are near you or far away. You will also learn how to talk about one thing or many things.

sections.p: Use 'this' when you talk about one thing that is close to you. For example, a pen in your hand. Use 'these' when you talk about two or more things that are close to you. Both words are for things near your body or right in front of you.

ex.mean: The coffee is in my hand or right here.
The shoes are on my feet right now.

sections.p: Use 'that' when you talk about one thing that is far from you. For example, a car down the street. Use 'those' when you talk about two or more things that are far away. Both words are for things you cannot touch easily.

ex.mean: The house is over there, far away.

ex.en: Look at those birds in the tree.
ex.mean: The birds are far up in the tree.

tip: Look at your hands! If you can touch it, use 'this' or 'these'. If you must point far away, use 'that' or 'those'.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct word for one item near you
quiz.en: ___ is my phone in my hand.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct word for many items far away
quiz.en: Look at ___ stars in the night sky.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct word for one item far away
quiz.en: Whose car is ___ parked down the street?

quiz.ask: Choose the correct word for many items near you
quiz.en: I like ___ apples I am holding.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct word for a near object
quiz.en: Is ___ your jacket on the chair next to you?

quiz.ask: Choose the correct word for far away plural objects
quiz.en: I want to buy ___ shoes in the shop window across the street.
